title: Gwilliams et al. 2023 — Introducing MEG-MASC: a high-quality magneto-encephalography dataset for evaluating natural speech processing
description: MEG-MASC provides raw magnetoencephalography recordings from 27 English speakers who listened to about two hours of naturalistic stories from the Manually Annotated Sub-Corpus (MASC), interspersed with random word lists and comprehension questions. Each participant completed two sessions, and word and phoneme onsets and offsets are time-stamped in the event metadata. The dataset is organized in BIDS and serves as a benchmark for large-scale encoding and decoding analyses of temporally resolved brain responses to speech.
methods_description: Participants listened to four synthesized fictional stories over two ~1h MEG sessions, with story order varying across participants. Speech was synthesized with macOS text-to-speech using three female voices and varied speech rates, and split into ~3 min audio files. Word and phoneme timings were derived by forced alignment with the gentle aligner.
